q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of steel wire rope?
title: Steel wire rope carbon footprint per tonne
short: Start with the wire rod per tonne of rope and the steel supplier's figure. Add drawing, galvanising if used, stranding, closing and lubrication energy, then divide the plant's energy by tonnes dispatched.

ul: Fibre or steel core and lubricant.
Drawing rod into wire with heat treatment.

p: Report per tonne by construction and finish. Galvanised rope adds zinc and the galvanising line.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per tonne (one month)
lines: Plant total: 172,750 / 3,000 = 57.6 kg CO2 per tonne
Add wire rod and zinc for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
